heroData.title: Hire in China (No Entity)
heroData.subtitle: Labor Dispatch
heroData.description: Complex 'Labor Dispatch' rules apply. EOR handles the mandatory '5 Insurances + 1 Fund' compliance.

steps.title: Contract
steps.description: Written contract MANDATORY within 1 month. Penalty: double salary.

steps.title: Handbook
steps.description: Employee Handbook (Staff Regulations) must be acknowledged.

steps.title: Medical
steps.description: Pre-employment health check often required.

items.title: Open-Ended
items.text: After 2 fixed-term contracts, the 3rd MUST be open-ended.

items.title: Termination
items.text: Unilateral termination is extremely difficult. Mutual separation is norm.

items.title: Social Medical Insurance
items.text: Mandatory for Chinese nationals. Covers basic public hospital visits (Tier 1-3 hospitals). Long wait times, basic drugs only.

items.title: VIP Wards
items.text: Public insurance does NOT cover the 'International/VIP' wings of public hospitals. Expats almost always need commercial insurance.

items.title: Commercial Insurance
items.text: Essential for retention of senior talent. Plans like MSH or Ping An Health cover private clinics (United Family) and direct billing.

items.title: Cost Shock
items.text: International Schools (IS) in Shanghai/Beijing are among the most expensive in the world. Expect 200,000 - 350,000 RMB per child/year.

items.title: Eligibility
items.text: Strictly for foreign passport holders. Chinese nationals generally cannot attend pure international schools (SAS, WAB).

items.title: Debentures
items.text: Some top schools require a 'Debenture' (interest-free loan) or Capital Levy of 50k+ RMB upon entry.

items.title: Labor Dispatch (Laowu Paiqian)
items.text: The strict legal term for EOR. Regulated by the Labor Contract Law (2013 Amendment). Limited to temporary (6mo), auxiliary, or substitute roles.

items.title: FESCO
items.text: Foreign Enterprise Service Company. Originally state monopolies for hiring staff for foreign rep offices. Now a generic term for large HR providers.

items.title: Co-Employment Risk
items.text: If EOR staff are treated exactly like internal employees (direct management, discipline), courts may deem a de-facto employment relationship with the client.

items.title: Severance (N+1)
items.text: Statutory severance applies even to EOR employees upon contract expiration or termination. 'N' is years of service.

items.title: 2-Year Limit
items.text: Fixed-term labor dispatch contracts must be at least 2 years. Dispatch agencies are the legal employer.

items.title: MOHRSS Portal
items.text: Official Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security website for latest regulations.

items.title: Labor Contract Law 2013
items.text: English translation of the amendment regarding Labor Dispatch limits.

items.title: Shanghai Social Insurance
items.text: Calculator for employer/employee contributions in Shanghai municipality.

steps.title: 15th
steps.description: Tax & Social Security filing deadline.

steps.title: Calculations
steps.description: Complex 'Cumulative Withholding' method for IIT.

steps.title: Annual
steps.description: Annual IIT reconciliation (March-June) for employees.

rows: Merged with Med in some cities.

items.title: Pension
items.text: Employer ~16% / Employee 8%.

items.title: Housing
items.text: Employer 7% / Employee 7% (rates vary 5-12%).

items.title: Fapiao System
items.text: Allowance for Housing, Meals, and Laundry can be tax-exempt for expats if official 'Fapiao' (invoices) are provided.

items.title: 13th Month
items.text: The '13th Month Salary' is customary (often paid before Lunar New Year) but not legally mandatory unless written in the contract.

items.title: Heating/Cooling
items.text: State-mandated operational environment allowances (High Temp/Heating) apply in certain provinces and seasons.

steps.title: New Year (Jan 1)
steps.description: 1 day off. Public holiday.

steps.title: Spring Festival (Jan 28 - Feb 4)
steps.description: Chinese New Year. 8 days off. The most important holiday. Offices shut down completely.

steps.title: Makeup Days
steps.description: To create long holidays, employees often work on adjacent Saturdays/Sundays. e.g., Jan 26 (Sun) and Feb 8 (Sat) are working days.

steps.title: Qingming (Apr 4-6)
steps.description: Tomb Sweeping Festival. 3 days.

steps.title: Labor Day (May 1-5)
steps.description: 5 days off. Another 'Golden Week' for travel.

steps.title: National Day (Oct 1-8)
steps.description: Combined with Mid-Autumn Festival for 8 days. The primary 'Golden Week' of the year.

items.title: Gongjijin (Housing Fund)
items.text: Mandatory savings for home purchase. Generally 7-12% contribution from both employer and employee. Tax-deductible.

items.title: Shebao (Social Security)
items.text: Collective term for the 5 mandatory insurances: Pension, Medical, Unemployment, Maternity, and Work Injury.

items.title: IIT (Individual Income Tax)
items.text: Progressive tax rate from 3% to 45%. Residents are taxed on worldwide income after 6 years.

items.title: 13th Month Pay
items.text: Customary annual bonus paid before Spring Festival. Not statutory, but highly expected by white-collar workers.

items.title: Fapiao
items.text: Official invoice generated from the tax bureau system. Required for all business expense reimbursements.

items.title: China Tax Bureau (STA)
items.text: State Taxation Administration portal for policy updates and electronic tax filing.

items.title: IIT App
items.text: Official mobile app for individual income tax filing and annual reconciliation.

items.title: Social Insurance Rates 2024
items.text: Comprehensive table of contribution rates for major cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen).

items.title: Annual Audit Checklist
items.text: Requirements for the mandatory annual tax and compliance audit.

items.title: Exemption
items.text: Standard monthly deduction is 5,000 RMB for all individuals.

items.title: Progressive Rates
items.text: Rates range from 3% to 45% based on annual cumulative taxable income.

items.title: Tax Benefits
items.text: Foreigners can still claim certain tax-free allowances (housing, child education) under specific conditions until end of 2027.

items.title: Preferential Tax
items.text: One-time annual bonuses can be taxed separately from monthly salary to lower the overall tax bracket.

items.title: Timing
items.text: Usually paid before Chinese New Year. Must be reported in the month of payment.

steps.title: Calculation
steps.description: Calculate gross, social deductions, and IIT by 5th of each month.

steps.title: Tax Filing
steps.description: Submit IIT returns via the Golden Tax system by the 15th.

steps.title: Disbursement
steps.description: Local payments to employees should arrive by the 10th or 15th.

heroData.title: WFOE Setup
heroData.subtitle: Wholly Foreign
heroData.description: Wholly Foreign Owned Enterprise. Standard structure for doing business. RO (Rep Office) is limited.

steps.title: Name Approval
steps.description: AMR (Market Supervision) name reservation.

steps.title: Business Lic
steps.description: 5-in-1 Business License issuance.

steps.title: Carving
steps.description: Carving of Company Chops (Official Seal, Finance Seal, etc.).

steps.title: Bank
steps.description: Open RMB Basic Account and Foreign Capital Account.

items.title: Chops
items.text: Physical chops are the legal signature. Guard them with your life.

items.title: Supervisor
items.text: Must appoint a Supervisor (cannot be Director/Manager).

items.title: The Big Fund
items.text: Massive state investment (ICF) to drive self-sufficiency in chip manufacturing. Key hubs: Shanghai (Zhangjiang), Wuxi, Hefei.

items.title: Legacy Chips
items.text: China dominates the 'Legacy Node' (28nm+) market, essential for automotive and IoT, while pushing hard for 7nm breakthroughs.

items.title: Guochanhua
items.text: The aggressive push for 'Localization'. Foreign suppliers are being systematically replaced by domestic alternatives where possible.

items.title: Mature Nodes
items.text: While advanced AI chips are restricted, China is rapidly expanding capacity in 'legacy' chips (28nm+) used in autos and IoT.

items.title: NEV License
items.text: New Energy Vehicles get free green license plates in restrictive cities like Shanghai, a huge purchase incentive.

items.title: Price War
items.text: Intense competition (BYD, Tesla, Nio) has led to a brutal price war. Margins are thin for suppliers.

items.title: Price War
items.text: Margins are razor-thin. Survival depends on scale and vertical integration (like BYD making its own batteries).

items.title: Infrastructure
items.text: Government subsidies have shifted from car purchases to building charging infrastructure and battery swapping stations.

items.title: Solar Dominance
items.text: China controls >80% of the global solar supply chain. Manufacturing costs have plummeted.

items.title: Energy Storage
items.text: Battery storage (CATL) is the new growth engine as the grid struggles to absorb renewable capacity.

items.title: Energy Storage
items.text: As renewables grow, the grid needs stability. The energy storage market (batteries, pumped hydro) is booming.

items.title: Solar Dominance
items.text: China controls >80% of the global solar supply chain. Competition here is fierce; look for niche components/materials.

items.title: Made in China 2025
items.text: Strategic plan to move from low-end assembly to high-tech manufacturing (Robotics, Aerospace, Biotech).

items.title: Lighthouse Factories
items.text: China hosts the highest number of WEF 'Lighthouse Factories' globally, showcasing advanced AI/IoT integration.

items.title: Robotics
items.text: China buys more industrial robots than the next few countries combined. Labor shortages are driving rapid automation.

items.title: SMEs
items.text: Even smaller factories are digitizing ('Little Giants' program) to connect to industrial internet platforms.

items.title: Scope
items.text: Integrates Hong Kong, Macau, and 9 Guangdong cities (Shenzhen, Guangzhou, etc.) into a world-class cluster.

items.title: Talent Tax
items.text: Qualified foreign talent in the GBA can enjoy a 15% IIT cap, subsidizing the difference from the standard 45% rate.

items.title: Talent Subsidy
items.text: Foreign talent working in the 9 mainland GBA cities can get a tax refund, effectively capping their Individual Income Tax at 15%.

items.title: Connectivity
items.text: The High-Speed Rail connects HK West Kowloon to Shenzhen Futian in 14 minutes. It is a true '1-hour living circle'.

items.title: General Trade
items.text: Standard import/export. You own the goods, pay duties/VAT, and can claim VAT rebates on exports (rates vary 0-13%).

items.title: Processing Trade
items.text: Import raw materials bond-free to re-export finished goods. Strict control by Customs (Handbook system).

items.title: Classification
items.text: China's HS Code system matches international standards (first 6 digits) but adds local sub-codes (8-10 digits). Misclassification leads to delays.

items.title: CIQ
items.text: China Inspection and Quarantine (CIQ) inspections are mandatory for many goods (food, cosmetics) and can take weeks.

items.title: Super Ports
items.text: Shanghai (Yangshan) and Ningbo-Zhoushan are the world's busiest container ports. Automated terminals run 24/7.

items.title: Bonded Zones
items.text: FTZs (Free Trade Zones) allow storing goods without paying duty until they enter the domestic market. Ideal for regional distribution.

items.title: Unmatched Ecosystem
items.text: Despite rising costs, no country matches China's component supply chain depth. You can find every screw, chip, and cable within a 50km radius in Shenzhen.

items.title: Resilience
items.text: Maintain a backup supplier in Southeast Asia to mitigate geopolitical or tariff risks.

items.title: WFOE
items.text: Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise. The most common investment vehicle, allowing 100% foreign control without a local partner.

items.title: Legal Representative
items.text: The person with the broad power to represent the company. Their name appears on the business license. Holds significant liability.

items.title: Company Chop
items.text: The official red seal. It has more legal weight than a signature. Possession of the chop equals control of the company.

items.title: Business Scope
items.text: A defined list of activities the company is permitted to undertake. Strictly enforced; operating outside scope is illegal.

items.title: Supervisor
items.text: A mandatory role (individual) who oversees the directors and finances. Cannot be a director or senior manager.

items.title: SAMR Portal
items.text: State Administration for Market Regulation. Registry for all Chinese companies.

items.title: Negative List 2024
items.text: Official list of sectors restricted or prohibited for foreign investment.

items.title: 5-in-1 License Sample
items.text: Example of the consolidated Business License (YYZZ) required for operations.

items.title: Bank of China Guide
items.text: Requirements for opening a corporate capital account (FDI account).

heroData.title: Recruitment
heroData.subtitle: Liepin & Boss
heroData.description: Local platforms (Liepin, Boss Zhipin) dominate. LinkedIn is limited (no social feed).

items.title: Boss Zhipin
items.text: Dominated by direct chat. Managers chat directly with candidates before interviewing. Essential for tech/younger talent.

items.title: Liepin
items.text: The go-to for mid-to-senior level talent. Focuses on headhunters and experienced hires.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.text: LinkedIn is severely limited in China (no social feed). It is primarily used by candidates looking for overseas jobs.

items.title: Standard Fees
items.text: Retained search fees range from 20-25% of annual gross salary. Critical for senior hires as 'guanxi' (network) matters.

items.title: RPO
items.text: Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) is popular for mass hiring (e.g., sales teams), often costing significantly less per head.

steps.title: Autumn Recruitment (Qiu Zhao)
steps.description: The golden season. Occurs Sep-Oct. Most graduates secure offers then.

steps.title: Spring Recruitment (Chun Zhao)
steps.description: Supplementary season (Mar-Apr). Pickings are slimmer.

steps.title: Hukou
steps.description: Top grads often prioritize employers who can offer 'Hukou' (residency) in Beijing/Shanghai.

items.title: Social Insurance
items.text: Employers must budget for 30-40% on top of base salary for social insurance and housing fund. Candidates focus on 'Pre-tax' (Shui Qian) vs 'After-tax' (Shui Hou) figures.

items.title: 13th Month
items.text: Annual bonuses (13th or 14th month) are standard for white-collar roles. They are typically paid before the Spring Festival.

items.title: Housing Fund
items.text: The 'Gong Ji Jin' (Housing Fund) is a critical benefit for young professionals. Rates vary by city (up to 12% contribution by both sides).

heroData.title: China HR Tech
heroData.subtitle: WeChat Integration
heroData.description: Local tools (Beisen, GaiaWorks) integrate with WeChat Work / DingTalk.

items.title: Alibaba DingTalk
items.text: The dominant enterprise app. Used for clock-ins, approvals, and internal comms. Any HRIS must sync with DingTalk APIs.

items.title: WeChat Work
items.text: The corporate version of WeChat. Preferred by MNCs. Essential for employee self-service and document distribution.

items.title: Mini-Programs
items.text: Modern payroll and HR tools in China are often delivered via WeChat Mini-Programs rather than standalone apps.

items.title: Data Localization
items.text: The Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) requires employee data to be stored within China. Cross-border transfers require security assessments.

items.title: Consent
items.text: Explicit consent is needed for processing sensitive personal info (medical, financial). HRIS forms must include compliant consent clauses.

steps.title: GPS Clock-In
steps.description: DingTalk/WeChat Work allow GPS-verified clock-ins. Standard for office and remote staff.

steps.title: Facial Recognition
steps.description: Highly common in manufacturing. Must follow local privacy guidelines for biometric data collection.

steps.title: Overtime Approval
steps.description: Digital workflows are used to track and approve overtime, critical for meeting the 36-hour monthly cap.

items.title: Beisen (Italent)
items.text: The leading local HR SaaS provider. Strong on recruitment and performance management modules.

items.title: GaiaWorks
items.text: Specializes in workforce management (WFM) for large retail and manufacturing teams.

items.title: Workday Integration
items.text: While Workday is used by HQ, many China branches use a 'local layer' for statutory compliance and mobile integration.

heroData.title: Fapiao Mgmt
heroData.subtitle: Golden Tax
heroData.description: Fapiao (official invoice) system is unique. 'Golden Tax' digital system rollout is ongoing.

steps.title: Legal Rep Presence
steps.description: The Legal Representative often must appear in person (with ID/Passport) to open the account.

steps.title: Site Visit
steps.description: Bank officers will often physically inspect your registered office address to ensure you exist.

steps.title: Chops
steps.description: You need the Company Chop, Finance Chop, and Legal Rep's Personal Chop to transact.

items.title: Basic Account
items.text: You can only have ONE Basic Account (Jiben Hu). This is the only account that can withdraw cash.

items.title: General Accounts
items.text: You can have multiple General Accounts (Yiban Hu) for loans or inter-company transfers, but no cash withdrawals.

items.title: Capital Injection
items.text: Foreign capital MUST be registered with SAFE (State Administration of Foreign Exchange). Converting USD to RMB is strictly controlled.

items.title: Dividends
items.text: Repatriating profits requires tax clearance. You must confirm all CIT has been paid before sending money out.

items.title: Golden Tax IV
items.text: The new system (fully digital) connects banks, tax bureaus, and companies in real-time. Discrepancies are flagged instantly.

items.title: Expense Claims
items.text: Employees must submit official Fapiao (invoices) for reimbursement. A credit card slip is NOT a valid tax voucher.

steps.title: Overtime
steps.description: Must pay 150% (weekday), 200% (weekend), 300% (holiday).

steps.title: Leave
steps.description: Statutory annual leave starts low (5 days) but increases.

steps.title: Unions
steps.description: Trade Union fee (2% of payroll) often mandatory.

items.title: One Month Rule
items.text: A written contract must be signed within 1 month of start date. Failure results in paying DOUBLE salary for every month of delay.

items.title: Language
items.text: The Chinese version prevails in court. Bilingual contracts are standard practice but ensure the translation is accurate.

items.title: The 2-Term Rule
items.text: After a prospective employee has completed two fixed-term contracts (e.g., two 3-year terms), the third contract MUST be open-ended (permanent).

items.title: Probation
items.text: Max 6 months probation for contracts of 3+ years. You can only terminate during probation if you can PROVE incompetence against set KPIs.

items.title: Standard Formula
items.text: Severance = N (years of service) × Monthly Average Salary. Capped at 3x the local average salary if high earner.

items.title: +1 Notice
items.text: If 30 days' notice is not given, an additional month of salary (+1) must be paid in lieu of notice.

items.title: Standard System
items.text: 8 hours/day, 40 hours/week. Strict overtime pay applies (1.5x/2x/3x).

items.title: Comprehensive System
items.text: For seasonal work (e.g., manufacturing), hours are aggregated over a year. Requires approval from the local Labor Bureau.

items.title: Overtime Pay
items.text: 150% on weekdays, 200% on weekends, 300% on statutory holidays. Unlike the US, this is strictly enforced for non-management.

items.title: Flexible Hours
items.text: For senior roles, apply for the 'Comprehensive Working Hour System' to avoid strict daily overtime calculations.

items.title: 24 Hour Rule
items.text: Foreigners must register with the local police station (PSB) within 24 hours of arrival (or moving). Hotels do this automatically.

items.title: Residential Areas
items.text: If renting a flat, you must go to the police station yourself with your landlord's documents and lease.

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Failure to register can lead to fines (up to 2000 RMB) and, critically, denial of future visa renewals.

items.title: Online Systems
items.text: Cities like Shanghai and Beijing now offer WeChat Mini-Programs for self-registration, saving a trip to the station.

items.title: Z Visa (Work)
items.text: The only legal visa for employment. Requires a Work Permit Notification Letter before entry.

items.title: M Visa (Business)
items.text: Strictly for meetings and trade fairs. Performing actual work on an M visa is illegal and leads to deportation.

items.title: Z-Visa
items.text: Strictly tied to your employer. If you quit, your residence permit is canceled. Requires a degree + 2 years experience.

items.title: R-Visa
items.text: For 'Class A' Talent. Valid for 5-10 years, multiple entry, zero fees, and allows faster processing for family members.

items.title: First-to-File
items.text: China generally does not recognize 'prior use'. The first person to file the trademark owns it. File BEFORE you enter.

items.title: Software Copyright
items.text: Register your source code with the CPCC. It's affordable and crucial for proving ownership in infringement cases.

items.title: Trademark Squatters
items.text: Squatters register foreign brands in China hoping to sell them back at a premium. Register your IP *before* you even speak to a factory.

items.title: Software Rights
items.text: For software, register a 'Software Copyright' (chuzheng) with the Copyright Protection Center of China (CPCC) to protect your code.

items.title: The Red Chop
items.text: In B2B contracts, the Company Chop (Red Seal) is the ultimate authority. A signature by a manager without the chop is often invalid.

items.title: Scanning
items.text: Verify the chop's serial number (often searchable online) and ensure it's not a 'Contract Chop' if the deal involves finance.

items.title: Identifying the Chop
items.text: It must be circular, red, and contain the full Chinese registered name of the company. A 'Financial Chop' or 'Contract Chop' has limited power.

items.title: Legal Rep
items.text: Only the Legal Representative (listed on the business license) has the statutory authority to sign contracts if the Chop is missing.

items.title: N+1
items.text: Standard severance formula. N months of salary for N years of service, plus 1 month in lieu of notice.

items.title: Open-Ended Contract
items.text: A permanent contract. Must be offered after 10 years of service or 2 fixed-term contracts.

items.title: Employee Handbook
items.text: Must be democratically consulted with staff to be legally binding. Critical for termination grounds.

items.title: Overtime Rules
items.text: 1.5x for workdays, 2x for weekends, 3x for statutory holidays. Strictly enforced in labor arbitrations.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Max 6 months for contracts of 3+ years. Salary during probation cannot be less than 80% of agreed wage.

items.title: Labor Contract Law
items.text: Full text of the PRC Labor Contract Law (English/Chinese).

items.title: Handbook Template
items.text: Standard structure for a compliant Employee Handbook covering discipline and leave.

items.title: Termination Notice
items.text: Sample notice form for mutual termination agreement.

items.title: Work Permit Guide
items.text: Classification criteria for Category A, B, and C work permits for foreigners.

items.title: High-Tech
items.text: HNTE status gives 15% CIT rate.

items.title: GBA
items.text: Greater Bay Area (Shenzhen) has specific talent subsidies.

items.title: Headline Rate
items.text: Hainan Free Trade Port offers a capped 15% CIT (Corporate Income Tax) and IIT (Individual Income Tax) for qualified sectors/talent.

items.title: Zero Tariffs
items.text: Imports of production equipment and raw materials are duty-free. Huge potential for processing trade.

items.title: The Benefit
items.text: Qualified R&D expenses can be deducted at 200% pre-tax. If you spend 1M RMB, you deduct 2M from taxable income.

items.title: Documentation
items.text: Strict project management and accounting separation required. 'Hiding profits' in R&D is a major audit trigger.

items.title: Tech SME Status
items.text: You need to apply for 'Tech SME' (Ke Ji Xing Zhong Xiao Qi Ye) status. It is easier to get than 'High-Tech Enterprise' status.

items.title: Audit
items.text: Keep meticulous records of R&D spend. The tax bureau audits this aggressively to prevent fraud.

steps.title: VAT Invoicing
steps.description: Issue Fapiao (official tax receipts) for all revenue using the Golden Tax system.

steps.title: Monthly Filings
steps.description: File VAT, Surcharges, and Individual Income Tax (IIT) by the 15th of each month.

steps.title: Quarterly CIT
steps.description: File Corporate Income Tax (CIT) returns based on quarterly profits.

steps.title: Annual Audit
steps.description: Complete statutory annual audit and CIT reconciliation (Huijiaqingsuan) by May 31st.

heroData.title: Contracts
heroData.subtitle: Chinese Language
heroData.description: Contracts must be in Chinese to be enforceable. Bilingual versions common.

items.title: Guanxi (Relationships)
items.text: Business is personal. Contracts are often viewed as a starting point for negotiation, not the final word. Trust is built over dinners, not in boardrooms.

items.title: Mianzi (Face)
items.text: Never cause a partner to lose 'face' (embarrassment) in public. Criticism should be subtle and private. Direct confrontation destroys deals.

steps.title: Seating
steps.description: The host sits facing the door. The guest of honor sits to the host's right. Never sit until directed.

steps.title: Toasting (Ganbei)
steps.description: If you toast, you must finish your glass ('Dry Cup'). Toast superiors with the rim of your glass lower than theirs.

steps.title: The Bill
steps.description: The host always pays. Fighting to pay is polite, but the host must win.

items.title: Language Clause
items.text: While contracts are written in both English and Chinese, the Chinese version almost always prevails in local courts. Professional legal translation is non-negotiable.

items.title: Dual Columns
items.text: Standard practice is to use a side-by-side dual-column format to ensure clarity for both HQ and local management.

items.title: Arbitration
items.text: CIETAC (China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission) is preferred for foreign contracts over domestic courts.

items.title: Litigation
items.text: Court proceedings are conducted in Chinese only. Foreigners need notarized and legalized POA (Power of Attorney) for legal representation.

items.title: Service Invention
items.text: Chinese law has specific rules for 'Service Inventions'. Ensure MSA clearly defines that inventions made during work hours belong to the employer.

items.title: NDA
items.text: Trade secret protection requires active measures (restricted access, locked cabinets). A contract alone is not 'protection' under Chinese law.

heroData.title: China Tech
heroData.subtitle: Great Firewall
heroData.description: Need specific tech stack (AliCloud, WeChat MP). Global tools (Google/FB) blocked.

items.title: No Google
items.text: Google, FB, Twitter, ChatGPT are blocked. You MUST have a compliant connectivity solution (IPLC or approved VPN) for office work.

items.title: Speed
items.text: International bandwidth is throttled. Utilize local CDNs (AliCloud/Tencent) for any customer-facing assets.

items.title: Roaming / eSIM
items.text: Using an international roaming plan (or Hong Kong eSIM) often bypasses the firewall automatically, unlike local Wi-Fi.

items.title: Commercial VPNs
items.text: Astrill and ExpressVPN are popular, but connectivity varies. Corporate leased lines (IPLC) are the only legal, stable option for offices.

items.title: Super Apps
items.text: Work happens on WeChat (Tencent) and Lark/Feishu (ByteDance). Email is secondary for many local teams.

items.title: Walled Gardens
items.text: Data doesn't flow freely between Alibaba (Taobao/DingTalk) and Tencent (WeChat) ecosystems. Choose your stack wisely.

items.title: Walled Gardens
items.text: Chinese internet is fragmented. Links from WeChat (Tencent) often don't open in Taobao (Alibaba). You must choose your ecosystem.

items.title: Super Apps
items.text: Meituan isn't just food delivery; it's bookings, hotels, and payments. ByteDance isn't just TikTok; it's e-commerce and education.

items.title: Data Onshoring
items.text: Personal data of Chinese citizens (PIPL) and 'Important Data' generally cannot leave China without a security assessment.

items.title: Local Clouds
items.text: AliCloud is market leader. AWS/Azure exist but are operated by local partners (Sinnet/21Vianet) to comply with laws.

items.title: ICP License
items.text: Internet Content Provider license. Mandatory for any website hosted in China. Two types: Commercial (rare for foreign firms) and Bei'an (standard).

items.title: Great Firewall
items.text: Google, Facebook, Twitter, and many foreign SaaS tools are blocked. VPNs are not a legal enterprise solution. Local hosting is required for speed.

items.title: PIPL Compliance
items.text: Personal Information Protection Law. China's GDPR. Strict data localization rules for cross-border transfer of personal info.

items.title: Cloud Providers
items.text: AliCloud (40% market share), Tencent Cloud, Huawei Cloud. AWS and Azure operate via local partners.

items.title: WeChat Mini Programs
items.text: Essential for consumer-facing apps. Lightweight apps that run inside WeChat, bypassing app stores.

steps.title: Entity Registration
steps.description: Secure a local business license to apply for digital services.

steps.title: ICP Bei'an
steps.description: Register your domain and server with MIIT to host content locally.

steps.title: Cloud Deployment
steps.description: Provision AliCloud or Tencent Cloud instances for low-latency access.

steps.title: Corporate connectivity
steps.description: Install IPLC or SD-WAN for stable access to global SaaS tools (Slack, Jira).

heroData.title: WeChat & Red
heroData.subtitle: Private Traffic
heroData.description: WeChat Official Accounts and Little Red Book (Xiaohongshu) are essential.

items.title: Baidu (Search)
items.text: The 'Google of China'. Essential for SEO/SEM. Requires a registered Chinese entity to open an ad account.

items.title: Tencent (Social)
items.text: WeChat is the operating system of life in China. Official Accounts (Service vs Subscription) are mandatory for brands.

items.title: ByteDance (Video)
items.text: Douyin (TikTok) is king for short video. Top priority for B2C consumer brands.

items.title: KOCs vs KOLs
items.text: Key Opinion Consumers (KOCs) are micro-influencers with smaller but higher-trust audiences. Often more ROI-positive than massive KOLs.

items.title: Little Red Book
items.text: Xiaohongshu (Red) is the platform for product discovery and reviews. Critical for lifestyle, beauty, and wellness brands.

items.title: WeChat
items.text: The Super App. Official Accounts (Service/Subscription) are the core of any B2C/B2B marketing strategy.

items.title: Douyin
items.text: Chinese TikTok. Dominated by livestream commerce. Essential for e-commerce and brand awareness.

items.title: Baidu SEO
items.text: Google is irrelevant. Baidu requires specific optimization strategies (hosting in China, simplified Chinese, ICP license).

items.title: Little Red Book (Xiaohongshu)
items.text: Social commerce platform. Critical for reviews, seeding, and influencer marketing (KOL/KOC).

items.title: Private Domain Traffic
items.text: The trend of moving users from public platforms (marketplaces) to owned channels (WeChat groups) for higher retention.

items.title: Tmall & JD
items.text: The titans of B2C. Opening a flagship store requires a local entity or a 'Tmall Global' offshore setup.

items.title: TPs (Tmall Partners)
items.text: Foreign brands usually hire localized agencies (TPs) to manage logistics, customer service, and marketing on marketplaces.

items.title: Live Streaming
items.text: Key for sales. TaoBao Live and Douyin are the primary channels. Requires significant investment in influencers.

steps.title: Livestreaming
